Header: Aphis spiraecola ( syn. Aphis croomiae ) Green citrus aphids, sabs Tela in Urdu language

Prevention: Excess nitrogen encourages new leafy growth that aphids love to feed on.
N, P, K at 1.5:1:0.8 kg only once at max.
Mn, Cu, Fe, Zn to improve plant defence.
Increase populations of natural enemies of aphids, for example tiny
Aphelinus wasps and ladybeetles through promotion of its habitats such as keeping flowering weeds or
Brassica that have other aphids as alternative hosts.
Monitoring: December as these are the vegetative growing seasons preferred by aphids.
Monitor weekly during sprouting stage, particularly checking the underside of leaves and stems.
Select trees randomly and count the number of shoots attacked by aphids.
Also note the level of natural enemies in a circle of 30 cm nearby aphids
Green aphids are up to 2 mm, tiny pear- shaped soft insects.
Some have transparent wings, many do not have wings.
Its body is bright greenish-yellow to apple-green.
If there are more than 5 to 7 aphids per most young leaves, then control action may be considered.
If there are many natural enemies, action may not be needed.
Control action may be too late when most leaves have heavily curled and became yellow with waxes on it.
Direct Control: Spray soap solution (Potassium soaps 10-15 tablespoons in a 16L knapsack).
Spray the orchards with a mixture of neem extract: water with few drops of soap.
Usually at 100 ml/ 100 lit. water, but check label.
